pages.name: A rule for the line
pages.text: The line from lesson 1 through A and B has a gradient of 2. Going back 1 from A to `x = 0` drops it 2, so it crosses the y-axis at 1, its [[intercept]] (also called the y-intercept or vertical intercept). From there each 1 along adds 2, so x along the line has climbed `2 × x` above 1: its rule is `y = 2x + 1`, and B fits it.

pages.name: On the line?
pages.task: Which point is on the line `y = 2x + 1`?
pages.why: Put each point's x into the rule and see whether you get its y. `2 × 3 + 1 = 7`, so (3, 7) is on the line. For (7, 3), `2 × 7 + 1 = 15`, not 3, and for (3, 6), `2 × 3 + 1 = 7`, not 6.

pages.name: Draw the line
pages.task: Drag the handles to draw `y = 3x − 2`: start at c, then step m up for each 1 along.
pages.why: `c = −2`, so the round c handle goes on the y-axis at (0, −2). `m = 3`, so from there the line climbs 3 for each 1 along, and the m handle sits at (1, 1), as `−2 + 3 = 1`.

pages.name: Number first
pages.text: In `y = 3 − 2x` the first number is not m: `3 − 2x` is 3 add `−2x`, and the two terms can swap places, so this is `y = −2x + 3`. m is the number multiplying x, with its sign, so `m = −2`, as y drops 2 each 1 along, and `c = 3`. Drag P: it lights only where `3 − 2 × x` gives its y.

pages.text: A faint copy of `y = 2x + 1` stays put while c slides to −3: every point drops the same 4, so `y = 2x − 3` runs alongside it, 4 below at every x. Lines with the same m and a different c are [[parallel]]. Slide c again, or turn m and the gap stops being the same.

pages.text: In `2y = 3x − 8`, y has a 2 in front. Halve every term, the 8 too, to get `y = 1.5x − 4`, so `m = 1.5` and `c = −4`. Drag either handle and both forms of the rule rewrite together.

pages.task: What are m and c for `4y = 8x − 12`?
pages.why: Divide every term by 4 to get `y = 2x − 3`. So `m = 2`, and `c = −3`, where the line crosses the y-axis. It crosses the x-axis at 1.5, where `y = 0`.

pages.name: The call-out
pages.task: Last one. Say a plumber charges a £40 call-out plus £30 for each hour (example values). Which rule gives the bill, y pounds, for x hours?
pages.why: The £40 is paid once, before any time passes, so it is c, where the line starts on the y-axis. Each hour adds £30, so `m = 30`. The rule is `y = 30x + 40`, and 2 hours cost `30 × 2 + 40 = 100` pounds.
